parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the principle of conservation of momentum.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
An object of mass $2m$ is travelling at a speed of $5.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in a straight line. It collides with an object of mass $3m$ which is initially stationary, as shown in Fig. 3.1.

{{figure:figure_3_1.png}}

Fig. 3.1

After the collision, the object of mass $2m$ moves with velocity $v$ at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ to its original direction of motion.

The object of mass $3m$ moves with velocity $w$ also at an angle of $30^{\circ}$, as shown in Fig. 3.2.

{{figure:figure_3_2.png}}

Fig. 3.2

By considering the conservation of momentum in two dimensions, calculate the magnitudes of $v$ and $w$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An object of mass $4.2\text{ kg}$ is travelling in a straight line at a speed of $6.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The object is brought to rest in a distance of $0.050\text{ m}$ by a constant force.

Calculate the magnitude of this force.
